medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: On occasion a student's normal progression may be interrupted by - illness, pursuance of another course of study or research, or personal reasons.  All requests for a leave of absence from the School of Medicine must be made in writing to the Assistant Dean for Student Affairs.  Leaves should be discussed with the student's counselor and the Student Affairs Dean, prior to submitting a formal written request. There are 3 types of leave of absence which students can request: Medical, Educational, or Personal.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Serving the community is at the heart of an education at WSU School of Medicine. Throughout the four years, students have the chance to participate and volunteer in more than 100 student-run organizations and free clinics.  

These organizations are devoted to many areas of student life, including community service, specialty-specific information, research, education, political issues in medicine, and many others. Each organization has a faculty advisor and receives financial assistance from our Alumni Association to host events for classmates and the greater community. 

All student organizations: https://www.med.wayne.edu/studentaffairs/student-orgs#definition-98152
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Wayne State University School of Medicine is positioned next to one of Detroit's largest hospital systems, Detroit Medical Center, and near Henry Ford Health System, Ascension Healthcare, and Corewell Health Dearborn (formerly Beaumont), taking experiences from the classroom straight to the hospital floor to serve the underserved.  

Minutes away from multiple neighborhoods in Detroit and surrounding cities, there is something for all individuals – nationally renowned restaurants, parks and public spaces, museums, and major sports teams. The diverse Metro Detroit area boasts unique cultural experiences and one-of-kind communities.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Detroit and the surrounding communities have many different housing options for students. Most students choose to live in apartments located close to campus, but there are lots of other options, including University-based housing and rental homes throughout Metro Detroit

Detroit and Housing: https://www.med.wayne.edu/admissions/detroit
University-based Housing: https://housing.wayne.edu/live/costs
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Wayne State University School of Medicine supports all students through its wide array of support services, which include counseling, mentoring, academic support, career advising, health and wellness initiatives, and more.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Office of Scholarships and Financial Wellness supports students with their transition and journey in Medical School. We offer a variety of useful information, resources, tutorials and assistance to ensure you are aware and stay on track for success. More at https://www.med.wayne.edu/servicecenter/financial-wellness

At Wayne State University School of Medicine, we believe that wellness is multi-factorial and fostered using evidence-based institutional initiatives accomplished through collaboration across undergraduate medical education (UME) departments, in partnership with medical students, and with the strong support of our leadership.  Our objective is to foster a culture of wellness with a learning environment that supports students directly addresses student concerns and facilitates the personal and professional development of our future physicians. Learn more at https://www.med.wayne.edu/studentaffairs/health-wellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At the Wayne State University School of Medicine, passion meets purpose. With endless opportunities to conduct research, accelerate health care and crucial work in our community, and contribute to the city’s culture and growth, Detroit is a place like no other. Our campus is buzzing with energy, offering the ultimate destination for you to learn and grow while connecting with others and experiencing new things. Our students are supported—by one another, and by our faculty, staff and alumni. And they go on to succeed. The experiences you'll have as a Warrior M.D. will help you excel anywhere.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Comprehensive academic advising, counseling, and tutorial services are integrated and coordinated through the Offices of Student Affairs and Learning and Teaching, all of which faculty oversight.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: In both pre-clerkship and clerkship years.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Emphasis on small-group case-based & problem-based learning. Small-group dissection labs in anatomy and extensive standardized patient-based learning in clinical skills during pre-clerkship.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin M2 year with a brief orientation followed by core clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures can be observed remotely. Attendance is required for small-group teaching and service endeavors.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The Wayne State University School of Medicine has a rich, 150-year history of preparing physicians and biomedical scientists who work to transform the promise of access to equal health care for all into a reality. Through hands-on clinical education in the heart of a rapidly-evolving city, the School of Medicine provides students a distinct experiential advantage.

The new Highways to Excellence curriculum develops more individualized educational experiences. The organ systems-based curriculum blends and reinforces basic sciences and clinical experiences from day one, integrating classroom, self-directed learning, and small-group learning with clinical skills, cases, experience, and training. The curriculum enables physicians-in-training to customize their studies with time for electives and career choice exploration, including opportunities to focus on the health of underserved populations through community impact missions and partnerships. 

More Info: https://highways.med.wayne.edu/overview
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
The pre-clerkship phase of the curriculum is aimed at facilitating self-directed learning, early clinical experiences, and opportunities to apply classroom learning within clinics and in the community. To give students an even greater start, we align the pre-clerkship curriculum to best take advantage of cadaver dissection opportunities for additional hands-on experience. 

Read more about pre-clerkship, clerkship and post-clerkship phases of the WSU SOM curriculum: https://highways.med.wayne.edu/overview/structure
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The School of Medicine's overall research programs are intimately focused on efforts to discover the bases of health conditions that negatively affect the lives of people in Michigan and elsewhere. Major opportunities exist in cancer biology, the neurosciences, cardiovascular pathophysiology, molecular medicine and genetics, women's health, pediatrics, and health disparities and population sciences. The school's clinical research programs are highly integrated with the basic science departments as well as with the research programs in the Henry Ford Health System. For more information, visit: https://medstudentresearch.med.wayne.edu/starting

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Founded in 1868, the Wayne State University School of Medicine is located in the heart of Detroit, Michigan with more than 1,000 medical students. In addition to undergraduate medical education, the school offers master's degree, Ph.D., and M.D.-Ph.D. programs in a wide variety of areas of basic science. Combined degree/M.D. degrees can also be attained including M.P.H. and M.B.A.

Wayne State University School of Medicine is known for its ability to develop clinical skills in medical students through one of the nation's most robust standardized patient programs and partnerships with leading hospital systems. Renowned faculty, a diverse patient population, and high-quality facilities are all vital factors that combine to make WSU a foundation of outstanding opportunities for medical training.

Learn more about urban- clinical- excellence at Wayne State University School of Medicine here: https://www.med.wayne.edu/admissions
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Wayne State, located in the heart of Detroit, provides a distinct experiential advantage that sets students apart from their peers and prepares them to be health care leaders and advocates. Our Highways to Excellence curriculum provides students with an organ systems-based curriculum, a focused clinical skills course, a deep and authentic understanding of health needs and challenges, multiple ways to take advantage of experiential service-learning, community engagement and research opportunities, and more. 

Our students have many opportunities to volunteer in the community, including at student-run free clinics, with area nonprofits, urban gardens, area schools and much more. Students also have access to a myriad of academic, financial, career and mental health support services designed to remove barriers and help them succeed as students, physicians, and health care leaders and advocates.  

Since 1868, the Wayne State University School of Medicine has educated and trained more than 26,000 highly-skilled and compassionate physicians, researchers and public health professionals. Our graduates are sought-after, and a large percentage serve in under-resourced communities. Our Class of 2024 achieved a 98.1 percent residency match rate, well above the national average, matching into 24 specialties in 30 states.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Letters should come from professionals who can assess your communication skills with patients and other professionals, your dependability, your professionalism, and your work ethic. Some examples include doctors you have shadowed, principal investigators or someone you have done research with, faculty advisors of clubs, or other health care professionals who can comment on your abilities to work with patients. Please review our updated policy at https://med-wayne-external.policystat.com/policy/17928243/latest/

ALL letters of recommendation must be submitted through the AMCAS Letter Service: https://students-residents.aamc.org/applying-medical-school-amcas/amcas-letter-service . Please be sure to review and share the AAMC guidelines with your letter writers.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
The Admissions Committee at WSUSOM requires a minimum of three (3) letters of recommendation with your secondary application. 

All letters of recommendation must adhere to AAMC AMCAS letter of recommendation guidelines and letter service must be used:  Section 6 of the AMCAS® Application: Letters of Evaluation | Students & Residents (aamc.org)

You may submit a statement from the pre-medical advisory committee at your college or university, or a minimum of three letters of recommendation — with at least two from faculty members, can be Principal Investigator (PI). One letter must have been written within the past 12 months.  

Letters more than three (3) years old will not be considered. Signature and letterhead is preferred. M.D./Ph.d program applications must submit a letter from a researcher. Applicants with a Post-baccalaureate or graduate GPA are required to submit at least one letter from their program.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: All interviews are conducted virtually and incorporate 3 different types of interviews, including a one-on-one faculty/alumni interview, a one-on-one medical student interview, and 5 MMI stations. Students will be provided with opportunities to take campus tours, and attend Q&A sessions and webinars with current medical students.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Financial aid awards administered by the School of Medicine are made by the financial aid officer based on federal guidelines and those established by the Committee on Financial Aid and Scholarships. The College Work-Study Program and other medically-oriented jobs are generally available to eligible students for the summer break. Financial aid seminars are held for incoming students. 

Additional information is available by visiting https://wayne.edu/financial-aid/medicine
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: The School of Medicine uses the credit hour method to charge for tuition and the omnibus fee.  The School of Medicine has resident and non-resident tuition and fees.  The majority of the students will register for and be assessed for 50 credit hours per year.  Various off-track students (e.g., modified students, those taking leaves)will register for variable credit hours.  If a student finds it necessary to withdraw from the University he/she should notify the Office of Student Affairs in writing.  If notice of withdrawal is sent by mail, the date of the postmark will be considered the effective date.  Any student seeking a leave of absence from medical school should contact his/her counselor for additional information. The cancellation of registration and refunds will depend on the dates the withdrawal/leave of absence is effective.

medSchoolPrograms.programLength: At Wayne State University School of Medicine we have a 5-year MD/MPH program. The program length varies with most students completing program requirements within 1 year. Students have up to 6 years to complete all degree requirements.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: In your AMCAS application, please select the combined medical degree-graduate and designate the MD/MPH program as your apply type.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The Pre-Medical Studies Graduate Certificate Program (Post-Bac) offers a rigorous, specialized curriculum designed for individuals seeking to enhance their academic preparation for a medical doctor program.

This program is a didactic, human biology-oriented curriculum involving primarily courses with content from several Basic Science departments and programs.

For more information, visit https://gradprograms.med.wayne.edu/premed-certificate

For more information about our combined degree programs please review our webpage: https://www.med.wayne.edu/admissions/degrees

In addition to the combined programs, Wayne State University also offers a  Three-Year M.D. program.  It is the only one of its kind in Michigan. Geared to fit students who have previous health care backgrounds and careers, the program diversifies the School of Medicine's offerings for students who are ready to accelerate their physician career by completing medical school and receiving a conditional, non-binding acceptance into a Wayne State residency position upon completion. All students accepted into the WSUSOM's MD program are eligible to apply for the Three-Year MD program. Learn more at: https://www.med.wayne.edu/admissions/application/three-year-md

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc:
Become a doctor one year sooner with Wayne State University School of Medicine's rigorous three-year M.D. program. This accelerated program is designed for highly motivated students with previous healthcare experience eager to launch their medical careers. 

The three-year M.D. program is available only to students accepted into the four-year M.D. program.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: The three-year M.D. program is available only to students accepted into the four-year M.D. program.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicant who receive a Waitlist decision will be reviewed for Acceptance by the Admissions Committee throughout the cycle.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: The Wayne State University School of Medicine has required and recommended coursework as listed in its premedical coursework policy, which is linked to at https://www.med.wayne.edu/admissions/support/policies . Please note, coursework is only one aspect of a student's application. It is advised that students reach out to their pre-health advisor to go over coursework before applying.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no expiry date on pre-requisite coursework, however courses must be completed at least three weeks prior to matriculation. Students should meet with pre-health advisor before applying.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Mission alignment review is the process used for the selection of applicants. Consideration is given to the academic record;  community service; patient care experiences; extracurricular activities and written responses using the AMCAS application, secondary application, and letters of recommendation as these reflect the applicant's personality, maturity, character, and suitability for medicine.  

As a state-supported school, the institution gives preference to Michigan residents; however, out-of-state applicants are encouraged to apply. Interviews are required but scheduled only with those applicants who are given serious consideration. Students are urged to apply by November 1.

Learn more about the WSU SOM and its policies at https://www.med.wayne.edu/admissions
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Prior quality experiences in the health care field is a desirable characteristic and improves your chances of being admitted to the Wayne State University School of Medicine, though it is not required.
